headline: All three BSC contracts are source-verified on BSCScan, but no public GitHub repo and no security audit from any recognized firm exist — meeting the red threshold on two independent axes.
short_headline: Verified bytecode, no repo, no audit

findings.text: All three pinned contracts verified on BSCScan via Etherscan source submission: BTCB token (0x7130d2a12b9bcbfae4f2634d864a1ee1ce3ead9c, BEP20Token, ABI source: etherscan), logic implementation (0xBA5Fe23f8a3a24BEd3236F05F2FcF35fd0BF0B5C, BEP20TokenImplementation, ABI source: etherscan), and factory (0x08adbaA6A215affd711F532ec219299ba1e5b9b7, ABI source: etherscan). No proxy.implementation pointer was returned for the BTCB token, confirming it is a direct (non-proxy) implementation. The factory's logicImplement() returns the verified implementation address 0xBA5Fe23f8a3a24BEd3236F05F2FcF35fd0BF0B5C.

No public GitHub repository is recorded in the protocol context (github: none) and none was discovered during this run. Source-to-repo correspondence cannot be established; no commit SHA can be pinned. This is a downgrade signal under the red rules ('no public repo').

No audit links are recorded in protocol.audit_links. A BSCScan search result for the BTCB contract page explicitly shows 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted.' No audit report from any firm was discovered via web search.

No audit from any recognized or unrecognized firm was found. The BSCScan contract page for 0x7130d2a12b9bcbfae4f2634d864a1ee1ce3ead9c explicitly states 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted.' The third-party claim of 'regular third-party code scans' (pp.one) cites no firm name, report URL, or date — not credible as audit evidence.
Post-audit drift cannot be assessed because no baseline audit exists. Omitted from scoring.

The BTCB token (0x7130d...) is a direct implementation — no proxy layer. The factory (0x08adb...) deploys upgradeable proxies pointing to the verified implementation (0xBA5F...). Both proxy and implementation are verified. No unverified implementation detected.

steelman.red: No public source-code repository is linked and no security audit from any recognized firm has been submitted — two independent red conditions per the grading rubric — making red the correct grade regardless of bytecode verification status.
steelman.orange: All three deployed contracts are source-verified on BSCScan, and the factory-to-implementation linkage is fully on-chain traceable; verification alone could support orange if one treated the absence of a repo and audit as 'partial' rather than 'absent.'
steelman.green: BTCB is a simple, widely-used BEP-20 token contract submitted to BscScan in September 2020 and in continuous production use; the contract code is minimal and has been battle-tested at scale, which a steelman might argue reduces audit necessity.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because two independent red conditions are satisfied: (1) no public source-code repository is recorded or discoverable, meaning V2 cannot be met, and (2) no security audit from any firm (recognized or otherwise) exists — confirmed both by the empty protocol.audit_links and by the BSCScan page explicitly showing 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted' for the primary BTCB contract. Bytecode verification (V1 satisfied for all three contracts) is a necessary but not sufficient condition for green or orange; the rubric requires ≥1 recognized-firm audit covering currently-deployed contracts, which is entirely absent here.

evidence.shows: BTCB token contract (BEP20Token) on BSC is verified on BSCScan (ABI source: etherscan). No proxy.implementation pointer returned — direct implementation. owner() and getOwner() return 0xF68a4b64162906efF0fF6aE34E2bB1Cd42FEf62d. Reads pinned to block 96967406.

Logic implementation contract (BEP20TokenImplementation) on BSC is verified on BSCScan (ABI source: etherscan). getOwner() returns 0x6e1C24586d0DFEB608E0442a8A1Ce772afEC03a6; mintable() returns true. Reads pinned to block 96967431.

Factory contract (Binance BEP-20 Token Factory) on BSC is verified on BSCScan (ABI source: etherscan). logicImplement() returns 0xBA5Fe23f8a3a24BEd3236F05F2FcF35fd0BF0B5C (the verified implementation). Reads pinned to block 96967432.

BSCScan token page for BTCB explicitly states 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted' and shows source submitted for verification on 2020-09-02. Confirms no audit has been submitted via BSCScan's audit registry.
Binance blog confirms BTCB is operated on a centralized and trust-based model, with BTC locked at a public address and BTCB minted/burned on Binance exchange. No audit mentioned.

unknowns: V2: No public GitHub repository found for Binance Bitcoin / BTCB BEP-20 contracts; source-to-repo correspondence and commit SHA pinning not possible.
V3: No audit links provided in protocol.audit_links; web search found no audit report from any firm covering 0x7130d2a12b9bcbfae4f2634d864a1ee1ce3ead9c or its factory/implementation.
V5: Post-audit drift assessment not possible — no baseline audit exists to compare against current deployment.

admin_addresses.role: owner of BTCB token contract (mint/burn authority)

protocol_metadata.about: Binance Bitcoin (BTCB) is a BEP-20 wrapped Bitcoin token issued by Binance on BNB Smart Chain, pegged 1:1 to BTC held in publicly disclosed Binance reserve addresses. Users deposit BTC on Binance to receive BTCB, which can then be used in DeFi applications such as lending, liquidity provision, and yield farming on BSC. The protocol operates on a fully centralized and trust-based model: Binance exclusively controls minting and burning via an onlyOwner mint function on the token contract. A factory contract (BEP-20 Token Factory) deploys upgradeable proxy instances using a shared implementation contract.
